contractEvidence.rule: Judge exact current repository hash from actual Store-card/detail pixels. SVG format is neither automatic approval nor failure; premium acceptance requires item identity, silhouette/fit, convincing materials and lighting, construction/hardware, theme/tier progression, card readability, originality and no inappropriate visual reuse.

reviews.name: Cloud Jacket
reviews.actualPixelFinding: The new hash cleanly decodes and is readable at card/detail scales, so the old v3 decode blocker is fixed. Identity is recognizable as a cloud-themed jacket and the zipper, pockets, cuffs and cloud/star motifs are clear. However the actual pixels are still predominantly symmetric/front-on flat-vector construction: sleeve and torso volumes do not turn convincingly in space, fabric/puffer loft reads as colored panels rather than tactile padded material, and lighting is mostly outline/gradient treatment instead of form-defining key/rim light. At Tier 4 it remains visibly less dimensional than the already accepted Tops 7-10 premium renders.
reviews.repairForProducer09: Keep this clean Cloud Jacket identity, Candy Core palette, zipper/pockets and cloud/star details, but rebuild the exact next version as a genuinely three-quarter garment: visible torso side plane, foreshortened far sleeve, rounded padded/quilted loft with seam compression, differentiated rib-knit cuffs/hem and believable zipper/metal response. Use a warm key plus cool rim/grounded shadow so volume survives Store-card scale. Do not simply add stronger outlines or recolor this same frontal vector recipe.

reviews.name: Star Coat
reviews.actualPixelFinding: The v4 hash cleanly decodes with no corruption, so the old v3 pixel-corruption defect is fixed. Adventure Club identity is stronger: navy/burgundy/gold palette, compass/star insignia, belt hardware, pockets and central quilting all read clearly. It still does not clear Tier-5 premium acceptance: the silhouette reads like a short bomber/field jacket rather than a long coat, the pose is nearly perfectly frontal/symmetric, and large fabric panels remain flat vector fills with limited tactile weave, thickness, folds or form lighting. A Tier-5 finale must be at least as physically dimensional and materially rich as the accepted lower-tier Tops, not merely more ornamented.
reviews.repairForProducer09: Preserve the clean Adventure Club navy/burgundy/gold language, compass/star identity and useful belt/pocket hardware, but make the next Star Coat unmistakably coat-length with a longer hem/tail and a three-quarter body turn. Add real fabric thickness at collar/hem, layered storm-panel depth, fold/tension cues, differentiated quilted vs woven vs metal materials, and stronger key/rim lighting with grounded shadow. Tier 5 should win on physical construction and material richness, not just badges and gold trim.
